questions.question: What is the core evidence invariant of NAS?
options: Candidates must use comparable versioned scoring, and finalists must be retrained independently of the search proxy
Every candidate must inherit the same weights
The largest search space always wins
Wall time and accelerator-hours are identical
questions.explanation: Comparable evidence prevents protocol drift, while independent retraining tests whether proxy or weight-sharing conditions created the apparent winner.

questions.question: A search consumes 8,000 accelerator-hours across 40 accelerators. Ignoring overhead, what is the wall time?
questions.explanation: Parallel wall time is total accelerator work divided by concurrent accelerators: 8,000 / 40 = 200 hours.

questions.question: Why can aggressive early stopping damage a search?
options: Early learning curves may rank architectures differently from full training and prune eventual winners
questions.explanation: Early stopping is safe only when the partial-training signal reliably preserves the decisions that full training would make.

questions.question: How does differentiable NAS represent discrete operation choices during search?
options: As a continuous weighted relaxation that is later discretized
questions.explanation: Continuous architecture weights make optimization differentiable, but relaxation and shared weights can bias the selected discrete architecture.

questions.question: What does low proxy-to-full rank correlation imply?
options: Search budget is being allocated using a signal that often selects the wrong candidates
The proxy is cheap enough for production
More candidates will automatically fix the proxy
The final architecture needs no retraining
questions.explanation: A proxy that reverses candidate rankings guides the controller toward measurement artifacts rather than full-training quality.

questions.question: Why use a Pareto frontier instead of one blended score?
options: It preserves independent trade-offs and prevents arbitrary weights from hiding a failed deployment constraint
It removes the need for latency measurement
questions.explanation: Hard gates should be enforced separately, and non-dominated candidates make quality/resource trade-offs visible to decision makers.

questions.question: How does repeated selection on one validation set create leakage?
options: The controller adapts to validation noise, so the set becomes part of the optimization signal
questions.explanation: Trying and selecting many candidates against one set overfits the architecture decision to that set. Final claims need untouched evidence.

questions.question: What is required before releasing a NAS-discovered model?
options: Fresh full-budget retraining, repeated seeds, matched hardware profiling, robustness checks, and comparison with strong baselines
questions.explanation: Production evidence must validate the actual discrete architecture under the real training, compiler, and serving conditions.
